---
title: "head() and tail() with n as text used to return the whole vector"
ref: DF-07
categories: [Data frames and lists]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "the first 3 or the last 3 elements"
versions: "Wrong result without error up to R 4.2, error since R 4.3.0"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022), R 4.3.0 NEWS"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
n <- "3"
head(1:10, n)
head(1:5, n)
tail(letters, n)
```
:::

Pick **R 4.1.3** in the menu, then run again: without any error, `head(1:10, n)` returns all ten values, `head(1:5, n)` the first three, and `tail(letters, n)` the whole alphabet.

## Why

An `n` stored as text slips in easily, for instance read from a parameter file or from a Shiny `input`. Up to R 4.2, `head()` did not check its type and computed `min(n, length(x))`. With text, `min()` compares strings in alphabetical order: `min("3", "10")` is `"10"`, because `"1"` comes before `"3"`. So the result depended on the length of the vector: right for 5 elements, wrong for 10. A data.frame suffered the same fate, `head(iris, "2")` returning all 150 rows.

R 4.3.0 turned this case into an error. An old script that "worked" may therefore stop after an upgrade, and that is a good thing.

## The fix

Convert the parameter to a number as soon as it enters the code.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
n <- as.integer("3")
head(1:10, n = n)
tail(letters, n = n)
```
:::
